answer: An AI-agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to maintain a unique onyx-sealed cryptographic relic that must be re-attested every epoch by a randomly sampled orchard of independent peers. The relic binds the agent's recent work history to a non-transferable key; failure to obtain the orchard quorum freezes voting weight. An attacker faces linear compute and stake costs per fake identity, because each clone needs its own relic refreshed by honest peers who reject duplicates, making large-scale identity farming prohibitively expensive over time.
